messages:
maya: Kicking off blue->green traffic shift for router-service v3.2 -> v3.3 in eu-west. Change window 02:00-02:30 UTC. Plan: ramp 0->5->15->35->65->100% in 3m intervals, drain old pods during each step. tagging @liz_ops and @sam for rollback hooks :rocket:
deploy-bot: Scheduled deploy: router-service v3.3 by maya at 2024-06-10T02:00Z. Canary instances up (3/3), health checks passing. Pins: route=canary:v3.3 -> will honor traffic weights. CI: green. Logs: https://ci.internal/1234
oncall-bot: Preflight checks: infra quotas OK, warm pool 12 GPUs, KV cache primed, certificate rotation verified.
sam: Quick question — are we pinning session affinity for the first 15m or allowing session stickiness to migrate?
maya: We'll keep session affinity on for the first two steps (0->5->15). After 15% we drop affinity to avoid hotspots. I'll add a note in release notes.
ryan: Rollback criteria proposal: immediate rollback if 95th p50 latency jumps >30% or 5xx rate >0.8% sustained for 2 consecutive windows (6m). Also rollback on model mismatch errors >0.5%. Thoughts?
liz_ops: +1 but also include error budget burn: if token-cost spikes >20% and customer impact visible, abort. Make sure console alert thresholds match these numbers. I can push the monitor thresholds now.
maya: Good. I'll open a small release checklist in the console: pinned version v3.3, health endpoints, metrics dashboards, and the rollback playbook link.
deploy-bot: Command executed: `routerctl set-weight --service router-service --version v3.3 --weight 5` -> OK. Current weights: v3.2=95, v3.3=5.
ryan: Can someone post the quick curl we use to sanity check the router after each increment?
sam: curl -sS -H "Host: router.internal" "https://eu-west-router/health?trace=1" | jq -r '.status, .latency_ms'  # use jq to pick latency
maya: First hold for 3m. Monitor p50/p95, error rate, and tail cache-miss. If any threshold trips, we pin back to 100% v3.2 and drain v3.3.
deploy-bot: Next step scheduled in 3m: set weight -> 15% (auto). Will post status after shift.
ryan: Make sure release notes mention: config change for header normalization, improved cache TTL, and a known fallback behavior for rare header-encoding case. Also note that the change is non-breaking for clients.
liz_ops: I've updated alert runbook and added an oncall rotation: if alert triggers, page ops-oncall and run `routerctl rollback --to v3.2 --force` then tag #incidents.
maya: Affirmative. I'll annotate the release notes with rollback commands and mark the change window.
deploy-bot: Shift complete -> v3.3=15%, v3.2=85%. Canary checks: p95 110ms (baseline 105ms), 5xx 0.03% (baseline 0.02%). All within thresholds.
sam: running the curl, looks healthy. No errors in logs.
ryan: watching dashboards. latency small bump is expected. Holding.
oncall-bot: Reminder: at +15m run `routerctl drop-affinity` per plan.
maya: After the 15% hold and another +3m smooth, we'll proceed to 35%. If anything odd, I'll call rollback. :thumbsup:
liz_ops: Thanks — I'll be standing by.
maya: Proceeding to 35% now. deploy-bot please?
deploy-bot: Command executed: `routerctl set-weight --service router-service --version v3.3 --weight 35` -> OK. Current weights: v3.3=35, v3.2=65. Canary checks: p95 118ms, 5xx 0.04%. No anomalies.
ryan: p95 trending up but within our 30% threshold. continuing watch.
maya: If everything looks stable we finish roll to 100% in the remaining steps. I'll update release notes with final version and tag support. Thanks team.
deploy-bot: Final shift scheduled as series of timed weight updates. Will report final success or rollback action.
